[[File:Triangle diagram of rewrite rule application svg.svg|thumb|Rewriting ''s'' to ''t'' by a rule {{math|1=''l''::=''r''}}. If {{mvar|l}} and {{mvar|r}} are related by a '''rewrite relation''', so are {{mvar|s}} and {{mvar|t}}. A '''simplification ordering''' always relates {{mvar|l}} and {{mvar|s}}, and similarly {{mvar|r}} and {{mvar|t}}.]]

In [[theoretical computer science]], in particular in [[automated reasoning]] about formal equations, '''reduction orderings''' are used to prevent [[endless loop]]s. '''Rewrite orders''', and, in turn, '''rewrite relations''', are generalizations of this concept that have turned out to be useful in theoretical investigations.

==Motivation==
Intuitively, a reduction order ''R'' relates two [[term (logic)|terms]] ''s'' and ''t'' if ''t'' is properly "simpler" than ''s'' in some sense.

For example, simplification of terms may be a part of a [[computer algebra]] program, and may be using the rule set { ''x''+0 → ''x'' , 0+''x'' → ''x'' , ''x''*0 → 0, 0*''x'' → 0, ''x''*1 → ''x'' , 1*''x'' → ''x'' }. In order to prove impossibility of endless loops when simplifying a term using these rules, the reduction order defined by "''sRt'' if term ''t'' is properly shorter than term ''s''" can be used;  applying any rule from the set will always properly shorten the term.

In contrast, to establish termination of "distributing-out" using the rule ''x''*(''y''+''z'') → ''x''*''y''+''x''*''z'', a more elaborate reduction order will be needed, since this rule may blow up the term size due to duplication of ''x''. The theory of rewrite orders aims at helping to provide an appropriate order in such cases.

==Formal definitions==
Formally,
a [[binary relation]] (→) on the set of [[term (logic)|term]]s is called a '''rewrite relation''' if it is [[closure (mathematics)#Closed sets|closed]] under [[context (term rewriting)|contextual embedding]] and under [[substitution (logic)#First-order logic|instantiation]]; formally: if {{math|''l''→''r''}} implies {{math|''u''[[term (logic)#Operations with terms|[]]''l''[[Substitution (logic)#First-order logic|σ]]]<sub>''p''</sub>→''u''[''r''σ]<sub>''p''</sub>}} for all terms  {{math|''l'', ''r'', ''u'',}} each path ''p'' of ''u'', and each [[Substitution (logic)#First-order logic|substitution]] σ. If (→) is also [[irreflexive relation|irreflexive]] and [[transitive relation|transitive]], then it is called a '''rewrite ordering''',<ref name="DJ90:251"/> or '''rewrite [[preorder]]'''. If the latter (→) is moreover [[well-founded]], it is called a '''reduction ordering''',<ref name="DJ90:270">Dershowitz, Jouannaud (1990), sect.5.1, p.270</ref> or a '''reduction preorder'''.
Given a binary relation ''R'', its '''rewrite [[Closure (mathematics)#Binary relation closures|closure]]''' is the smallest rewrite relation containing ''R''.<ref name="DJ90:252">Dershowitz, Jouannaud (1990), sect.2.2, p.252</ref> A transitive and reflexive rewrite relation that contains the [[Term (logic)#Operations with terms|subterm]] ordering is called a '''simplification ordering'''.<ref name="DJ90:274">Dershowitz, Jouannaud (1990), sect.5.2, p.274</ref>

==Properties==

* The [[converse relation|converse]], the [[symmetric closure]], the [[reflexive closure]], and the [[transitive closure]] of a rewrite relation is again a rewrite relation, as are the union and the intersection of two rewrite relations.<ref name="DJ90:251">Dershowitz, Jouannaud (1990), sect.2.1, p.251</ref>
* The converse of a rewrite order is again a rewrite order.
* While rewrite orders exist that are total on the set of [[Term (logic)#Ground and linear terms|ground term]]s ("ground-total" for short), no rewrite order can be total on the set of [[Term (logic)#Formal definition|all terms]].<ref group=note>Since ''x''<''y'' implies ''y''<''x'', since the latter is an instance of the former, for variables ''x'', ''y''.</ref><ref name="DJ90:272">Dershowitz, Jouannaud (1990), sect.5.1, p.272</ref>
* A [[rewriting#Term rewriting systems|term rewriting system]] {{math|{{mset|1= ''l''<sub>1</sub>::=''r''<sub>1</sub>,...,''l''<sub>''n''</sub>::=''r''<sub>''n''</sub>, ... }}}} is [[termination (rewriting)|terminating]] if its rules are a subset of a reduction ordering.<ref group=note>i.e. if {{math|''l''<sub>''i''</sub> > ''r''<sub>''i''</sub>}} for all ''i'', where (>) is a reduction ordering; the system need not have finitely many rules</ref><ref name="DJ90:270"/>
* Conversely, for every terminating term rewriting system, the [[transitive closure]] of (::=) is a reduction ordering,<ref name="DJ90:270"/> which need not be extendable to a ground-total one, however. For example, the ground term rewriting system { ''f''(''a'')::=''f''(''b''), ''g''(''b'')::=''g''(''a'') } is terminating, but can be shown so using a reduction ordering only if the constants ''a'' and ''b'' are incomparable.<ref group=note>Since e.g. {{math|''a''>''b''}} implied {{math|''g''(''a'')>''g''(''b'')}}, meaning the second rewrite rule was not decreasing.</ref><ref name="DJ90:271">Dershowitz, Jouannaud (1990), sect.5.1, p.271</ref>
* A ground-total and well-founded rewrite ordering<ref group=note>i.e. a ground-total reduction ordering</ref> necessarily contains the [[term (logic)#Operations with terms|proper subterm]] relation on ground terms.{{#tag:ref|Else, ''t''&#124;<sub>''p''</sub> > ''t'' for some term ''t'' and position ''p'', implying an infinite descending chain ''t'' > ''t''[''t'']<sub>''p''</sub> > ''t''[''t''[''t'']<sub>''p''</sub>]<sub>''p''</sub> > ...<ref name="DJ90:271"/><ref>{{cite tech report| author=David A. Plaisted| title=A Recursively Defined Ordering for Proving Termination of Term Rewriting Systems| year=1978| number=R-78-943| pages=52| institution=Univ. of Illinois, Dept. of Comp. Sc.| url=https://archive.org/details/recursivelydefin943plai}}</ref>|group=note}}
* Conversely, a rewrite ordering that contains the subterm relation<ref group=note>i.e. a simplification ordering</ref> is necessarily well-founded, when the set of function symbols is finite.<ref name="DJ90:272"/><ref group=note>The proof of this property is based on [[Higman's lemma]], or, more generally, [[Kruskal's tree theorem]].</ref>
* A finite term rewriting system {{math|{{mset|1= ''l''<sub>1</sub>::=''r''<sub>1</sub>,...,''l''<sub>''n''</sub>::=''r''<sub>''n''</sub>, ... }}}} is terminating if its rules are subset of the strict part of a simplification ordering.<ref name="DJ90:274"/><ref>{{cite journal | author=N. Dershowitz | title=Orderings for Term-Rewriting Systems | journal=[[Theoret. Comput. Sci.]] | volume=17 | number=3 | pages=279–301 | url=http://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~nachum/papers/Orderings4TRS.pdf | year=1982 | doi=10.1016/0304-3975(82)90026-3 | s2cid=6070052 }} Here: p.287; the notions are named slightly different.</ref>
